This value is calculated directly in the **Medium & Calibration** field of the Sound Level module channel setup. This should not be confused with the **Maximum Sound Pressure Level**, which always includes a time-weighting filter that influences the measured peak value. results.title: What is the relationship between loudness and amplitude? - Definition & Definition | CK-12 Foundation
results.content: # What is the relationship between loudness and amplitude? The relationship between loudness and amplitude is that loudness is the perception of the strength of a sound wave, while amplitude is a measure of the physical strength of the sound wave. Specifically, the amplitude of a sound wave is directly related to the energy it carries and its intensity, and the higher the amplitude, the greater the intensity of the sound. Loudness is a subjective experience that depends on the amplitude of the sound wave as well as the frequency and individual hearing sensitivity. In general, as the amplitude of a sound wave increases, the loudness of the sound also increases. However, the relationship between loudness and amplitude is not linear, as the human ear perceives loudness on a logarithmic scale. This is why sound intensity levels are measured in decibels (dB), a logarithmic unit. Can larger amplitudes of light and sound produce brighter colors?
